candidates.snippet:
Indian Coast Guard vessel and tanker in distress Indian Coast Guard patrol ship assisting the tanker in distress (Ministry of Defense)
By The Maritime Executive 2026-09-28 11:31:48
A specialized damage control team from the Indian Coast Guard was able to arrest the flooding endangering a product tanker off the northeastern coast of India in the Bay of Bengal. The Chinese-owned vessel was being taken in tow to a secure anchorage off Paradip, India, for additional repairs.
The Coast Guard received a distress call from the tanker Sea Gull 9 (11,131 dwt) early on Saturday morning, September 27. The vessel was approximately 37 nautical miles east-southeast of Paradip and reported uncontrolled flooding.
Built in 1998, the tanker is registered in Belize and has a crew of 23 aboard. It is 127 meters (417 feet) in length.
The tanker was coming from Malaysia bound for Paradip with a cargo of 9,000 metric tons of palm oil.
The crew reported a main engine failure. Pictures released by the Coast Guard show the vessel listing to port and low in the water.
Sea Gull 9 was taking on water after a reported main engine failure (ICG)
The Indian Coast Guard patrol boat ICGS Vishwast responded and deployed a damage control team to the tanker. The team deployed submersible de-flooding pumps, stopped the leak, blanked two damaged seawater pipelines, and contained a third fractured line. They were able to eliminate the immediate threat of the vessel sinking.

Two of the VLCCs are the Tifani (IMO 9273337), a 300,000 dwt tanker falsely claiming registry in Botswana, stopped in April in the Indian Ocean, and the Majestic X (IMO 9198317), a 281,500 dwt tanker falsely claiming registry in Guyana, which was stopped two days after the first tanker, also in the Indian Ocean.
Both of these vessels were detected sailing north along the coast of Brazil. Both were laden with Iranian crude and made it out of the Persian Gulf, likely heading for China, before the blockade was first imposed in April 2026.
The Pentagon asserted the vessels were stopped under the right of visit, inspecting sanctioned stateless vessels.
Combined, the three ships would be laden with approximately six million barrels of Iranian crude. That would be a value of roughly $600 million based on current market prices. Only the Majestic X , briefly in late July, showed a destination of the United States, according to Kpler’s data.
Observers, however, are confident the ships are headed toward the United States, likely Texas, where the U.S. will enforce its forfeiture.
The Trump administration has spoken about the possibility of seizures.

Crude oil began flowing again on Saturday from Iraq’s semi-autonomous Kurdistan region to Turkey, marking the first shipment in over two years after an interim agreement ended a prolonged deadlock, Iraq’s oil ministry confirmed.

The Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline had been shut down in March 2023 after the International Chamber of Commerce ordered Turkey to pay USD 1.5 billion in damages for unauthorized exports managed by Kurdish authorities.
Under the preliminary agreement, the KRG will supply at least 230,000 bpd to Iraq’s state oil marketer SOMO, while reserving 50,000 bpd for local consumption, officials familiar with the deal said. An independent trader will handle sales at the Ceyhan port using SOMO’s official pricing.
The eight companies involved in the deal and the KRG have agreed to meet within 30 days of the pipeline’s reopening to finalize a mechanism for settling outstanding debts.

Low-cost aerial threats can arrive in volume, and meeting each one with a premium interceptor is an equation no navy can sustain.
